Current Limitations and Roadmap Status

This page honestly lists the parts of SLA that are not yet stable or are deliberately not done: mutability forms, lowering coverage for aggregates/enums/derive/for-in/async, no-fallback progress, and the real state of the rosetta example tree. After reading it, you can avoid mistaking “planned” for “guaranteed”.

Mutability: &mut Not Introduced

Per the v0.2 revision of rust_surface_compat_report_cn.md, the Phase 1 stage introduces no mut form at all; SLA's &self convention covers both Rust's &self and &mut self, backed after lowering by the SA Referee (examples such as demos/rosetta/59_method_counter have verified this). &mut T/&mut self are planned for a later stage; let mut, by contrast, will never be introduced — it conflicts with SLA's current “let is mutable by default”. Do not use these forms in code.

Surfaces Not Yet Fully Covered by direct SAB

roadmap_status_cn.md §2 (snapshot 2026-07-01) assigned the tests still failing in the no-fallback scan at that time to their Phases, corresponding to user-visible feature categories:

Feature categoryGap at the timeOwning Phase
Enum payload / match extractionenum_match: tag/payload layout and match extractionPhase 5
Derive semanticsderive_semantics: operator/function calls generated by derivePhase 5
Struct update / comparison operatorsstruct_update, spaceship_cmpPhase 5
The for in protocolfor_in_protocol, generic_for_in_protocol: non-generic and generic iterator specializationPhase 6
async / awaitasync_await: single/double await, join2, linear chains of three/four consecutive awaits, and some Pending/Ready state machines have landed; nested await across async fn boundaries and a unified executor/reactor are still gapsPhase 8 (partially complete)
Call and assignment cleanupassign_move_cleanup, etc.: coordinating UseAfterMove with assignment/loop cleanupPhase 3
WarningSyntax being parsed and passing check does not mean that feature's direct SAB path is stable. Code in the categories in the table above may take a slower fallback path, or error directly in no-fallback mode.

How to Read the no-fallback Progress Numbers

  • roadmap_status_cn.md (v0.1, 2026-07-01): the no-fallback sweep was 58/69 (about 84%), Y/shared-lowering about 72%, direct SAB fallback elimination about 88%, and the weighted overall progress about 80%.
  • direct_sab_historical_69_corpus.md (evidence refreshed 2026-07-12): all 69 historical unit-test files are still present, and both the local and installed-plugin strict direct-SAB no-fallback scans passed 134/134 (the current test set has grown to 134 files).
NoteThe two sets of numbers use different bases: the former is a progress snapshot with a failure list, the latter is a later full scan of the expanded test set. When citing them, state the source and date; do not merge them into a single “current pass rate”.

The rosetta Example Tree Does Not All Pass

demos/rosetta/ is a work surface still in progress, not proof that “300+ demos all compile and pass”:

  • sa_std_macro_gap_audit.md states explicitly that the audit targets the rosetta demos and that “demos still must be rewritten and verified manually” — demos still need to be rewritten one by one and verified manually; the audit's purpose is only to surface common std macro/lowering gaps early;
  • Some demos already serve as measured evidence for specific capabilities (such as 07_trait_vtable, 40_impl_block_state, 59_method_counter, 55_builder_pattern), as well as 301-304, newly added for operator overloading;
  • The audit document also records surfaces still to be filled in, such as storage for owned trait objects and broader coercion positions, which are “future work” rather than completed items.

Other Boundaries Worth Knowing

  • union syntax can be parsed, but its robustness is considered less mature than struct/enum;
  • There is no stable user-defined Drop trait and no defer; cleanup is inserted by the compiler at scope exit;
  • There are no Rust-style associated types, const generics, or where clauses; fixed-size arrays [T; N] are not const generics;
  • Support for escaping heap-allocated closures should still be regarded as limited;
  • The maturity of the for in protocol for generic containers is lower than direct indexing or explicit container methods.

Network Protocol Capability Status (2026-09-19)

ProtocolStatusNotes
TCP / UDP / Unix socket✅ Availablenet.sai, plus the io_uring reactor netx.sai
TLS client✅ Availablesa_std/tls_client.sai, pure Zig std.crypto.tls, system CA + SNI + hostname verification, no off switch
WebSocket client✅ Availablesa_std/ws_client.sai, pure Zig RFC 6455; wss:// reuses the TLS client
HTTP/2✅ Availablesa_std/http2.sai, libnghttp2 driven via dlopen
IPv6✅ AvailableThe client layer natively supports it via tcpConnectToHost; [::1] has been measured
HTTP/3 / QUIC❌ Skeleton onlysrc/runtime/sa_quic.zig has only capability probing (dlopen looking for ngtcp2/nghttp3); the protocol state machines for connections/streams/ACK etc. are not implemented
SSH client❌ NoneNo implementation at all; if it is to be added, start with an exec channel with password/publickey authentication
DTLS client❌ NoneThe existing sa_dtls.zig is a DTLS server-side capability wrapper, not a client

The HTTP/3 trade-off: its benefits concentrate in weak-network / high-packet-loss / cross-network switching scenarios (0-RTT, connection migration, no TCP head-of-line blocking); on stable machine-room-to-machine-room networks HTTP/1.1/2 is sufficient, and no consumer is currently blocked by it.
